title: Make `bullet demo` work without a working directory or an env var
body:
An operator ran `bullet demo` from `~/bullet` and got:

```
bullet: open ledger: ledger: SQLite path contains an empty or non-normal component
```

That reads as a corrupt install. It is two separate papercuts.

**The default was relative.** `data_dir()` fell back to `./target/demo`, so where the ledger resolved depended on the working directory; from a directory with no `target/` the custody check rejects the path. It now defaults to an absolute private path under `XDG_STATE_HOME` (or `~/.local/state`), and `BULLET_DATA_DIR` still wins.

**`demo` created the directory group-writable.** It used `fs::create_dir_all`, which applies the umask — a default 002 yields `0775`, and the ledger then correctly refuses it with `SQLite immediate state parent must be euid-owned exact 0700`. `farm init` already creates its directory privately via `ensure_private_data_dir`; `demo` now does the same.

Verified: from `~/bullet` with no environment set, `bullet demo` creates `~/.local/state/bullet/ledger` at `drwx------`, writes receipts, and exits on its honest `COMPONENT_ONLY` note. `bullet` unit tests 64/64, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

title: Paint colours the terminal can actually render, and keep the hints visible
body:
An operator ran `bullet tui` and reported it as *"dark red against black … really bad"*, and that it was *"NOT obvious what to do"*. Both are real defects with a single first run behind them.

**Colour.** `tui.rs` chose colour on `NO_COLOR` alone and then emitted 24-bit RGB unconditionally. On a terminal that does not advertise truecolor — a plain `screen.xterm-256color` with `COLORTERM` unset, the common case under screen and tmux — the navy ground `Rgb(8,16,31)` quantises to black and the amber chrome `Rgb(255,196,77)` lands on a muddy dark red. That is precisely the reported symptom.

This adds a `Palette` with three representations and picks one from the terminal's own advertisement: truecolor when `COLORTERM` says so, otherwise indexed ANSI with the ground left to the terminal so the console sits in the operator's theme rather than fighting it with a near-black it cannot reproduce. `NO_COLOR` still wins and still paints every cell `Reset`.

**Guidance.** The bottom bar replaced the key hints with the error text, so the single line naming `Ctrl+K`, `Tab`, `j/k` and `?` vanished exactly when a confused operator needed it — on a first run with no daemon, the screen was an error, empty panes, and no hints at all. The error now renders above the hints instead of in place of them.

Verified: `operator_tui` 4/4 pass, `bullet` unit tests 64/64 pass including the assertion that `NO_COLOR` leaves every cell `Reset`, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

title: Open the default operator TUI and preserve authenticated work identities
body:
Running bullet or bulletfarm without arguments opens the operator TUI. Keep navigation and detach responsive during credential discovery, display validated operator records without waiting for command discovery, and add Fleet, Ready Queue and Outbox panes with actual server identities. Improve midnight/cyan/amber rendering, ANSI/NO_COLOR fallback, persistent shortcuts and operator help.

Bind authenticated reads and command/revoke mutations to the expected session acknowledgement before consuming responses. Keep submission records separate from execution rows and preserve exact reconnect subjects. Retain fail-closed execution admission while reconciling earlier proposals.

Validation on f73a657: complete canonical local required passed 1,280 selected fast tests, 34 contract tests, five additional preservation tests, lint, security and docs. All seven hosted required checks passed. The installed developer binary from product commit d9b1ace passed both-alias PTY startup/help/palette/detach checks; actual native Tuiwright passed all 12 scenarios. Later changes affect fixtures, CI policy and documentation. Terminal tests reserve capacity while retaining six concurrent clients per scenario and existing deadlines. Historical failed runs remain preserved; excluded host-dependent cases receive no passing credit.

The durable task composer, executing Head, supervised native provider sessions and signed installed service remain incomplete. This branch conflicts with main and needs reviewed reconciliation plus independent approval. Component UI evidence is not live-provider or release acceptance.

title: Document how to actually run and use Bullet
body:
The README opened on `just fast` and a simulator demo. That answers "how do I
prove this checkout", not "how do I use this". Someone who runs `bullet tui`
first — which is what the operator did — had no way to learn what the panes
are, which keys do anything, or why the screen is empty.

Adds an operator tutorial covering prerequisites, starting the console,
authenticating without putting a token in argv, the full TUI keymap, what each
view reads, the web Portal, and seeding a ledger so the views are not empty.

It states plainly what does not work yet — a submission is accepted and then
settles `UNKNOWN`, and neither surface can approve, retry or cancel — and adds
a troubleshooting table for the refusals a first run actually produces
(`FARMD_REQUEST_FAILED`, `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `TUI_TERMINAL_REQUIRED`, `NODE_PIN`,
the 0700 ledger custody refusal).

Every command in it was run on a real host before it was written.

Verified locally: `ops/ci/docs-check.sh` (14 files), `ops/ci/docs-freshness.sh`
(4 documents), and `route_inventory_binds_router_readme_and_openapi` all pass.

title: Allow concurrent credential readers and release status locks before HTTP
body:
Concurrent CLI and TUI readers could reject one another with AUTH_BUSY because every credential load took an exclusive lock. An auth status request also held that lock while waiting for the daemon.

Read-only consumers now load credentials under a short shared lock and release it before HTTP. The shared guard cannot escape as a writable store. Login, revocation, forgetting credentials and journal writes retain exclusive custody; active writers still produce AUTH_BUSY. Directory identity is checked around successful loads, and existing ownership, permissions, symlink, hardlink, schema and size checks remain in force.

Three regressions cover six overlapping readers, writer exclusion and displaced state, and an actual status request waiting on a withheld HTTP response. The measured inventory is 1,292 total / 1,246 standalone; removing the three new identities reproduces both previous inventory hashes exactly. No tests were removed or reclassified.

Validation: focused CLI tests and strict Clippy passed. Full clean-commit required run passed: 1,246 standalone tests, 34 offline contract tests, lint/meta checks, security, generated-contract drift, rustdoc and documentation links. Simultaneous Tuiwright qualification on xbabe2 remains separate; this change does not claim native-provider or installation readiness.

title: Persist operator conversations with exact retry and owner-scoped recovery
body:
Human messages now persist as operator-owned conversation threads through POST /api/v1/commands. Exact retries recover the original receipt, competing appenders use the accepted message cursor, and authenticated paged reads let clients rediscover threads after local cache loss.

Schema 27 atomically records the message, command, audit event and reference-only head-turn request. Admission validates immutable history and backup/restore preserves the records. Generated Rust, TypeScript, JSON Schema and OpenAPI agree. The generic coding runner cannot consume these requests; the response means message saved. A native conversational head and CLI/Portal chat consumers remain separate work (HEAD_RUNTIME_BINDING_REQUIRED).

The CLI also rejects duplicate JSON members before mapping HTTP responses or private journals, including nested and escaped-equivalent keys, without echoing private input.

Validation on e0e386f6d1e09ed5bce7b2f3aac5c6893423da57: complete local required lane passed (fast: 1,243 component tests; lint; contract: 34 tests; security; docs). Added 22 exact test identities cover rollback boundaries, response loss, restart/discovery, competing clients, stale cursors, owner isolation, malformed history, migration and restoration. All changed source packets received independent static review. Native execution and installed-product evidence are not established by this PR; Operating HOLD remains.

title: Preserve unresolved Candidate finalization and use receipt-bound cleanup
body:
After preserving a Candidate, Runner now observes an acknowledged provider termination before releasing the attempt and performing receipt-bound cleanup. Cleanup no longer tries to mint a live lease permit after successful release. Failures during termination, required journal writes, release or cleanup return a typed `FINALIZATION_UNRESOLVED` error containing token-free preservation references and the original cause; they do not enter generic failure cleanup or issue a second release/requeue.

Regression fixtures cover negative termination acknowledgements, termination errors, release committed with its response lost, cleanup refusal, cleanup completed with its response lost, and failed required/recovery journal writes. They assert actual retained or removed workspace artifacts, preservation references, queue/lease state and zero or one release. Existing test identities remain; six tests were added to the audited inventory.

Validation: 110 Runner library tests pass; strict workspace/all-target Clippy and canonical inventory validation pass. The complete required lane on exact commit `bbcbea77de9bc8ab97822f62ebd3c17dc79c0297` passes: 1,221 standalone tests and 34 contract tests, plus lint, security, documentation and proof-custody checks. Independent source, fixture and inventory reviews accepted all 14 changed files.

Scope: this is component evidence. Native descendant observation, durable unknown-capacity retention beyond the existing lease TTL, atomic Candidate/Attempt/quota/verifier settlement, and end-to-end cleanup retry recovery remain open. The Operating HOLD remains in effect. Portal connected and packaged checks will be rerun with fresh accepted Runner/Gitd binaries after this change lands.

title: Persist operator-owned coding task intent and exact retry
body:
New coding submissions currently require callers to invent launch authority and do not retain a complete task contract. This change accepts closed `bullet.run-coding.v2` task intent through the authenticated command ingress, atomically preserving its owner, immutable revision, dependencies and server-derived run tracking.

The CLI journals before POST, supports exact saved-request retry and discovers accepted task subjects after local cache loss. Owner-scoped task reads validate request digests and report exact queue blockers. Fresh legacy authority-bearing submissions return a typed refusal; historical owned retries retain their original bytes and current phase.

Schema 26 is additive. Task acceptance does not allocate a nonce, reservation, lease or legacy dispatch claim. Runnable scheduling, monetary liabilities, native completion and the conversational CLI/web/Slack front door remain separate unfinished work. Portal's fresh-submission consumer still needs the new contract; this is not a daily-use or provider-execution milestone.

Validation: 20 new regression identities, none removed (1,261 total; 1,215 standalone). Focused model, adapter/migration, HTTP, CLI and real CLI-to-farmd router recovery tests pass. Generated Rust/TypeScript/JSON Schema checks, inventory meta-tests and strict all-target workspace Clippy pass. The complete required lane passes on `03aa7d9008dcc418c756e38a5f7ff954b372040f`: all 1,215 selected standalone and 34 contract tests, lint, security and docs. title: Read missions through authenticated operator snapshots
body:
`bullet mission list` and `bullet mission status --mission <id>` now read the authenticated daemon through the existing validated atomic operator snapshot. Each invocation retains the original sequence, timestamp and source, refuses malformed or missing subjects, and uses the private credential store without opening a local ledger. Optional `--farmd` must match the saved destination.

Explicit `mission status --data-dir <directory>` preserves local component inspection and rejects remote flags. Terminal output and errors use the existing control-character sanitization. Three actual CLI/HTTP fixture tests cover credentials, one read per invocation, malformed truth, missing missions, early subject/destination refusal and local-mode conflicts. The canonical inventory adds exactly those three identities (1,241 total / 1,195 standalone), with all prior identities and exclusions preserved.

Validation: nine focused mission tests and strict Clippy passed; source, inventory and documentation have independent static review. The first full required run stopped at an existing backup test timeout (106 passed, one timed out); that failure is retained. The same test passed in 5.5 seconds in isolation under the unchanged fast profile. These are authenticated component reads. They do not establish installed provider execution or change task submission, native controls, independent verification or release eligibility.

title: Reject ambiguous JSON before command admission
body:
Command payloads containing duplicate JSON fields previously collapsed to the last value before the daemon could reject the ambiguity. The command endpoint now uses the existing recursive strict JSON visitor through Axum's JSON extractor, then validates the closed command envelope before entering the ledger transaction. Content-type, body-size and authentication error protections remain in place.

A real local HTTP regression covers duplicate root, nested and escaped-equivalent keys, unknown envelope fields and trailing data. Each refusal preserves command, event and outbox state; a subsequent valid request can use the same key and replay its original result.

Validation on b1cf8f3df68931a85a2f2b3e495deebeb458edb1: ten focused HTTP tests and strict all-target Clippy passed. Full local required passed, including all 1,192 standalone tests, 34 contract tests, lint, security and docs. Push run 34434537685 and PR run 34434592659 passed all seven required checks each on this exact head.

This is command admission hardening. Task-shaped server allocations, scheduling and native lifecycle remain open; no live provider or release admission is claimed.

title: Add durable operator sessions, command recovery and a read-only TUI
body:
Operator clients previously lost their session on daemon restart and could not safely reconcile a submission after losing its response. The CLI also printed credentials, and composed operator views could mix different ledger snapshots.

This adds durable operator sessions and revocation, private bootstrap/credential files, operator-owned command discovery, exact journaled retries returning the original command's current phase, and authenticated atomic snapshots. The Rust CLI uses generated models and bounded response validation; the new read-only Ratatui console preserves selection and detaches without stopping work. Append-only migrations preserve historical commands without assigning them an inferred owner.

The matching Portal changes are neverhuman/bullet-portal#5 and its follow-up #6. This remains a component milestone: task-shaped server allocation, scheduling, native lifecycle controls, independent completion and persistent installation remain open. Operating HOLD remains effective.
